To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chlorarachniophage nucleomorph contains histone genes that are targeted to the nucleomorph and that the host cell nucleus contains histone genes targeted to the nucleus.
the chlorarachniophtye nucleomorph is complemented with nucleus‐encoded histone proteins and that the corresponding histone genes show cell cycle‐dependent regulation.

the chlorarachniophysal nuclear genome encodes two sets of histone genes of distinct origin, one for the nucleus and one for the nucleomorph, and that the nuclear histones are differentially regulated during the cell cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution and the molecular biology of the chlorarachniophage plastid, the complex plastid of secondary endosymbiotic origin, which is retained in a number of protists.
the molecular mechanisms underlying plastid endosymbiosis and the evolution of plastids.
the molecular biology of the chloroplasts of algae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chlorarachniophtye nucleomorph is an autonomous, self‐replicating subcompartment with its own genome, but with the host cell nucleus encoding the histone genes.
the nucleomorph is an autonomous genome, but that the nuclear genome is in control.
the nuclear genome has a major influence on the nucleomorph and its gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleomorph is a highly specialized subcellular compartment, which is maintained in a symbiotic manner.
the nucleomorph is not a self‐contained genome but rather an integral part of the host cell nucleus.
the nucleomorph is not as autonomous as we thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear genome is able to exert a high level of control upon its endocellular junior partner.
the nucleomorph has been reduced to a subnuclear compartment, but it has not been completely abandoned.
the nuclear genome of the host cell has been co‐opted for maintaining the nucleomorph genome.
